| R2 | Posterior over frame-of-best-focus as the merge's central object; confidence = entropy, occlusion = bimodality, "no frame in focus" = boundary mass | design | **SPLIT VERDICT, both halves now MEASURED. Bimodality ACCEPTED → [M21](../research/M21-occlusion-bimodality-measured.md); confidence-as-entropy REFUTED → [M32](../research/M32-posterior-confidence-measured.md).** *Bimodality:* multi-peaked curves are enriched **4.38×** at depth steps on `coffee-bean` (permutation placebo 1.01×; ~2.7× after stratifying out the intensity-gradient confound; 9.5–14.3× in the most textured quintile) — but the effect is undetectable on `109`/`119`, where noise alone flags 60% of pixels, so the detector is deployable only *gated on the calibrated noise floor*. Two constraints follow: bimodality needs a **finer scale** than the merge's focus window (invisible at R=13, present at R=2), binding R14; and M18 must retain sufficient statistics so it lands without a rewrite. *Confidence:* the self-normalised form is **blind and non-monotone** in the evidence (0.6480 → 0.6482 across a 6.1× evidence range; 9% response to a 16× SNR change against the calibrated arm's 22 orders of magnitude), and the **calibrated** form is **degenerate** — the through-focus peak stands at **142–991 σ**, so the posterior is a delta on real data. **The frame choice is not the uncertain part**, and confidence must come from the merged estimate's predicted σ, the acceptance-set width and the sub-frame peak offset instead (question 65). Also corrected: the no-information null is **0.874 at n=53, not 1.0**, and it drifts with `n` — the review's proposal as written would mis-threshold every short stack. **Third fold-in → [M34](../research/M34-confidence-vector-measured.md): entropy survives as ONE CHANNEL of a vector, never as the scalar the review proposed.** Per pixel the posterior is a delta for only **76.5%** of pixels (p99 = 4.74, max = 39.05), and the informative tail correlates with the true sub-frame deficit at **+0.3349** — so `n_eff` ships. But it cannot ship alone: the three real-valued channels flag near-disjoint pixel sets (union **14.278%** against a **15.0%** disjoint ceiling; every pairwise overlap at **0.53–1.35× chance**, against a label-shuffle null that returns chance to four decimals), and predicted σ is **anti**-correlated with the sub-frame deficit (worst-5% lift **0.89×**), so **no monotone scalar summary of them is faithful**. This also qualifies M32's own fact 261: it was measured on binned populations, and a median cannot falsify a claim about a tail |

| R4 | Metacalibrated alignment edges (per-edge response `R` from planted ±δ, divide by own `R`) | cheap | **REFUTED → [M23](../research/M23-metacalibrated-edges-measured.md). The review's highest-value item ships nothing, and its supporting evidence was an artefact.** Three independent kills. (a) *The premise fails:* metacalibration requires a response `R` that is a property of the edge, but the measured `R` swings **0.53 → 0.99 across the probe amplitude δ** on the same pair — there is no edge-intrinsic response to divide by, so the correction is a function of the arbitrary probe size. (b) *The mechanism is the plant, not the optics:* a **zero-defocus self-pair** — the same frame against itself, where the true response is exactly 1.000 by construction — reads **0.372**. The shrinkage fact 45 attributed to blur asymmetry is produced by the probe's own **bilinear resampler**, which is a lowpass. (c) *It changes nothing:* re-admitting corrected span-1/2 edges leaves held-out error at **6.758 px** against 6.760 px uncorrected. **Fact 45's causal reading is WITHDRAWN; its numbers stand** — they measure the resampler, not defocus. The reviewer's own pre-registered criterion (b) — "on `112MSDCF` the correction must be a measured no-op" — is what fired, in the form of the self-pair control |

| R7 | **(mean, max) dual focus response** for fact 73's monotone-edge blind spot, running max via van Herk/Gil-Werman | cheap | **MECHANISM CONFIRMED, REMEDY REFUTED → [M17](../research/M17-dual-response-measured.md).** The review diagnosed a real defect and prescribed the wrong cure. The blind spot is real and the `max` does cure it — but the `max` **costs +18.91 DN on occluding edges, 21.7× the pre-registered bar**, because a running max is exactly the statistic a bright defocused foreground dominates. The dual therefore ships the halo it was hired to avoid. **What ships instead is `tenengrad-sq-w13`** — an arm added as an afterthought, not proposed by the review — which cures the same blind spot (discrimination **1.0000 → 0.1860**), is quality-neutral (15/30 cells, p = 1.00), noise-neutral, and runs at **0.96× the cost** because squaring the gradient drops a per-pixel `sqrt`. **Answers question 100.** The reviewer's instinct — "the mean is blind because blur conserves total variation, so use a statistic that is not TV-conserving" — was right; `max` and `square` are both non-TV-conserving, and only one of them is robust |

| R9 | Per-frame photometric normalisation (gain + offset) in the forward model | small | **MEASURED — see [M24](../research/M24-photometric-drift-measured.md). Premise confirmed, and the requirement is sharper than stated.** Drift is real and widespread: **2.88% / 6.84% / 8.93% / 11.70%** peak-to-peak on four stacks, with the framing confound discharged (central-ROI ratios 1.50/2.05/0.92, r = +0.85…+0.97). The new part: **EXIF does not predict it in either direction** — two stacks vary 7–9% with a single distinct `(exposure, ISO, f-number)`, and on `coffee-bean`, which *does* change exposure mid-capture, the level moves **16% of what EXIF predicts** (1.0443 vs 1.2800). So the gain must be **fitted from the data, never read from metadata**, and since σ²(S) is signal-dependent the noise model has to see it. Dispatched to M18. **`109MSDCF` is the quietest stack at 0.91%** — the corpus this project measured on is the one that hides this |

| R11 | Hot pixels + dust from the 242 delivered darks; dust smears under warp | small | **MEASURED, both halves — [M22](../research/M22-hot-pixels-measured.md) (additive) and [M29](../research/M29-static-defects-measured.md) (multiplicative).** *Hot pixels:* a recurrence-derived map (agreement across the 11 ISO groups, not a σ cut) finds **11,393 real defects = 0.0346%** — but in real 1.3 s frames they displace a pixel by **+3.0 DN, i.e. ≤ 0.39σ**, flat across three signal decades. This sensor is clean; build the map, do not let it preempt the merge. **All 242 darks are 1/100 s while real stacks run 1/60 s–2.5 s**, so the map is complete for the wrong exposure (now `captures-needed.md` §6). *Dust:* the review's most attractive sub-claim — that an estimator dilutes a sensor-fixed shadow for free while a selector copies it whole — **is refuted. `D = 0.999` at `n_eff = 3`.** Suppression is bought by the **span** of frames averaged, not their count, and a focus merge averages **adjacent** frames precisely because they agree (M27: `n_eff ≈ 3`; M28: disagreement grows near-linearly with separation). Adjacent-frame warp is sub-pixel, **0.07–0.22 green px**; a 0.2 px shift does not move a shadow 10–40 px across. **So dust needs explicit handling, and it cannot come from subject frames**: the limit is a **32–50% shadow** against real dust of 1–15%, because the floor is *scene texture* and does not fall with frame count (exponent **+0.025** over a 16× sweep). Flats reach a **0.120%** floor at n=20 — **158× better** — which turns `captures-needed.md` §4 into a specification with σ figures attached. The review's warp-smearing claim remains untested and is still the right follow-up |

| R14 | Decide the fold's sufficient-statistics seam **before** the merge is written | design | **ACCEPTED, MEASURED, AND DECIDED → [M18](../research/M18-merge-implemented.md). The review's best structural call.** The seam is **two-pass over frames**, carrying **60 B/px constant in frame count** — decode is 0.91 s warm, so the second pass is cheap, and O(workers) memory survives. Two corrections to the review's framing. (i) It offered "define the statistics the single-pass fold carries **or** go two-pass" as equals; they are not, because bimodality needs a finer scale than the merge's own window (fact 152: enrichment **4.38× at r=2**, **0.36× — depleted — at r=13**), so the statistics must be gathered at **5×5, not 27×27**, and a single-pass fold at the focus window's scale cannot retain them at any budget. (ii) The seam was proved **non-perturbing by byte-identical SHA256** over 3516×2344×3 pixels with the placebo on — the gather changes nothing it does not intend to. This is now rule 26 |

Regions with a broad focus peak (low-magnification, small aperture, flat surfaces) get more SR; sharply-peaked regions get less. **Why this matters for a focus stacker — the actual mechanism.** A focus measure is a high-pass energy statistic. On a *textureless* patch, that energy is **pure noise**, and its expected value is a known function of local signal level. A naive "sharpest wins" merger therefore performs *argmax over noise* in flat regions — it systematically selects the noisiest frame, and the merged output ends up **noisier than any single input**. The prior project measured exactly this failure on this camera: stack output was **2.3–4.6× noisier** than the source frames' cross-frame σ in flat zones, and up to **1.82× more spatially noisy than a single source frame** in flat highlights (`C:\dev\macro\research\empirical_findings.md` §2b).

4. **The genuinely-new deliverable is not the Wiener merge; it is the occlusion-aware merge — and the novelty claim must be narrowed.** See §4. The two-layer occlusion model has been formulated and inverted at least six times in the vision literature (Asada 1995/1998; Bhasin & Chaudhuri 2001; Favaro & Soatto 2003; McGuire et al. 2005; Hasinoff & Kutulakos 2007; McCloskey et al. 2011), and Wang et al. 2015 give a working remedy for the bimodal case. **"First to model the occlusion halo" is false.** What survives is **"first shipping focus-stacking tool to model it"**, and that is worth stating carefully because a SIGGRAPH paper says the problem is open in general: *"depth estimation can fail, especially next to occlusion boundaries, which present a general problem for all computational extended-DOF systems … While a principled solution to this problem is beyond the scope of this paper, most artifacts can be eliminated with simple manual layer refinement."* (Levin et al. 2009, §5, full text — MEASURED as a statement of the field's practice: their fix is **manual**.)

Run six merge arms on **109MSDCF (22 frames)** and **119MSDCF (33 frames)**: (A) shipped noise-gated merge, (B) plain argmax, (C) plain mean, (D) guarded focus-axis regularised inverse filter with per-frame OTF from the through-focus curve width composed with the measured diffraction OTF and σ from the photon-transfer model, (D′) the same without the diffraction term, (E) the same unguarded. Score **only** on paired metrics that can fail in both directions — gradient *correlation* against a reference plus a flat-ROI noise ratio, never bare `mean |∇|` (fact 145) — restricted to the 15.1% of pixels M20 says are candidates (fact 142) *and* reported over the whole frame, *and* split at the measured cutoff `f_sig = 0.2762 cyc/px`. **Null control:** permute frame order before building the OTFs; the advantage must collapse to ~1.0× (M21's placebo read 1.01×). **Degenerate control, free:** `coffee-bubbles` is 19 frames at *constant* focus (fact 49), so arm D must reproduce arm C exactly or the implementation is broken. **Positive control:** a planted synthetic stack, built Forster-2004 style, where the estimator is known to win; if it does not win there, the harness is broken, not the idea. **Kill criterion, pre-registered:** if D does not beat A on gradient correlation on the candidate pixels below `f_sig` by a margin that survives the permutation null, *or* if D's flat-ROI noise exceeds A's at equal gradient correlation, *or* if the advantage vanishes when the OTF comes from an independent optical model instead of the through-focus curve, the estimator is dead as a merge and stays a plugin. * **P35 — MEASURED.** `through_focus.rs` already ships a posterior over frame-of-best-focus on the **identical calibrated temperature** as the merge gate — `temperature() = √2 · FOCUS_NOISE_SD` (line 313), with a doc comment stating the commensurability with `Gate::tolerance` deliberately — but on a **different kernel**: `through_focus.rs:371-373` computes `exp(−gap/T)`, **exponential**, while M111's `softgate.rs` computes `exp(−gap²/2T²)`, **Gaussian**. The codebase therefore now weights one z-axis three ways at one temperature: **top-hat** (`merge.rs`, shipping, decides bytes), **exponential** (`through_focus.rs`, diagnostic, `--stats` only), **Gaussian** (`softgate.rs`, opt-in, unreachable). The Gaussian is what a normal gap of sd `T` implies, which is what `FOCUS_NOISE_SD` was calibrated to describe; the exponential is heavier-tailed and admits far frames more readily — the direction that made `--gate 1e5` destroy the photograph. **That is an argument, not a measurement: both should be priced against the same ladder (P34) before either is integrated.**

I registered that account as gate **(c)** — *the lowest bin's mean will still exceed 2 %* — and it **FAILED**: at n=58 the lowest bin's mean is **1.89 %**, under the bar. The tail is real (mean exceeds median in **all seven** bins, 64.52 % against 8.04 % in the top one) but it is **not what sank run 1**. The real cause is the gate's own **bin boundary**: it averaged `D` < 1.5, and by `D` = 1.5 the arms already differ by half and the shift has climbed to 3.40 %. **My ‘low disparity’ band was too wide to mean what it said**, so the gate failed on threshold placement, not on statistic choice or sample size. With the strict lowest bin, mean and median **agree**, and the original mean-based gate would have passed.

* **P66 — MEASURED. On M111 data the family ordering is REVERSED — dispersion survives to *fewer* levels than location.** Dispersion (mean gradient energy) crosses 20 % at **N = 4**; location crosses 0.2 px at **N = 12**. This is not an artefact of comparing two thresholds in incommensurable units: swept over location tolerances 0.05–0.50 px against dispersion tolerances 5–40 %, the reversal holds on **83.3 % of 120 threshold pairs**. Normalising each family by the quantity it measures — location error over the 0.4357 px planted magnitude, dispersion error over full-depth energy — location is the worse-behaved family at **12 of 13** levels; the single exception is the bottom rung N = 2 (47.16 % against 51.53 %), and that gate was registered as *every* level and so **failed as written**. **Caveat, and it points the alarming way:** the normalisation is relative to the planted 0.4357 px, so a *smaller* displacement — such as the 0.155 px the project measures — makes location's relative error correspondingly **worse**, not better.

* **P70 — MEASURED, pre-registered at commit `4b6caf2` before the data existed. ORCH's `D` rule is CONFIRMED, and on a **second, independent family of statistic** it did not have.** ORCH's ladder was built from ratios of two **raw** gradient energies. M111 built a second family whose terms are themselves **within-arm inside/outside ratios**, so each term has already cancelled once before the outer division, and binned it the same way. Family Q median |shift| by `D`: **0.73 % / 1.07 % / 1.61 % / 3.24 % / 6.35 % / 7.05 % / 45.70 %** (n = 800/311/216/128/75/7/5), **monotone in every step**, against family R's **0.68 % / 0.90 % / 3.79 % / 6.15 % / 6.71 % / 7.58 % / 8.04 %** on the identical tiles. Restricted to matched high disparity (`D` ≥ 4) the two families agree to within **5 %** — R **7.87 %** (n = 769) against Q **8.28 %** (n = 31), a factor of **0.95**. **`D` governs regardless of composition depth.**

* **P73 — MEASURED, pre-registered at commit `e40f7d2` before the data existed. My own hypothesis — that ORCH's deterministic-quantisation mechanism transfers to spatial gradient statistics as a **level-dependent magnitude** effect — is REFUTED by my own registered gate.** Walking the level-count axis by window size, with n ≥ 187 at every rung, the ratio of equal-variance white dither to deterministic rounding of the same 256 DN step is **flat**: **2.22 / 2.12 / 2.56 / 2.50 / 2.38 / 2.47 / 2.14 / 2.08 / 1.95** across median level counts of **61 → 5601**, a **92×** span. H2 (≥ 3×) FAILED at 2.22× and H3 (monotone rise) FAILED; the registered **H5 self-refutation** arm fired. **ORCH's 16× is temporal and does not reproduce spatially at that size** — across frames the same scene value recurs exactly, so the rounding error is near-perfectly correlated; between neighbours it is correlated only where the local gradient is under the step.

* **P75 — MEASURED (observed in the same table; not separately gated). The deterministic perturbation does not average away with window size and the random one does.** Median gradient-energy change under dither falls **17.43 % → 3.70 %** from an 8 px to a 128 px window (256× more pixels), while under rounding it stays flat at **0.87 % → 1.80 %**. **The finding worth carrying, and it is not the ordering (P64).** The immunity ORCH cites is measured as a **bias**. Bias is a signed, pooled quantity, and it cancels. On these tiles at **N = 12** the signed bias reads **−0.0034 px** — an apparently perfect null — while the median per-window absolute deviation is **0.2060 px**. The bias is small there *because it is crossing zero*, and the crossing sits at the maximum of the scatter, so **the pooled statistic is at its most reassuring exactly where the per-window statistic is at its worst**. M111 made the same error in its own first pass and cites itself for it (P68).

**Why this is not academic for this project (P65).** The lateral-CA displacement M107 corrects and M113 re-measured is **0.155 px**. Per-window scatter passes that signal at **N = 16**, and by N = 12 **62.6 %** of windows are past it. A per-window CA fit on a low-contrast crop can therefore be reading noise larger than its own signal while a pooled bias check on the same data returns a clean null.

**Where it does show up, which is not where I looked (P74, P75).** Two signatures survive, and neither was what I gated on. **Sign:** rounding *removes* gradient energy in windows flat enough for neighbours to collapse onto one level, and dither cannot produce a negative change at all — **37.68 %** of 8 px windows disagree in direction, falling monotonically to 4.81 % at 128 px. **Averaging:** dither's effect falls 17.43 % → 3.70 % as the window grows 256× in area while rounding's stays flat at 0.87 % → 1.80 %. So a dither control on a gradient statistic is within a factor of two on magnitude — it *looks* calibrated — while getting the direction wrong on a third of small windows.

| 550 | **SUPERSEDED IN PLACE by M25's own second pass — the measurement stands, the diagnosis was wrong, and the advice this row gave was dangerous.** As folded, this row read that fact 14's two-level *read noise* under-predicts M4's measured dark sigma at ISO 50 by 45% (0.541 DN vs 0.987 DN), and advised re-fitting the read-noise term with a low-ISO branch. **The defect is in `g`, not `RN_e`.** Sony ISO 50 is an extended/pull setting: the sensor reads out at base-ISO-100 analogue gain, so `g = ISO/436.8` is **2.05x too small** there and, since `sigma^2 = g*S + (RN_e*g)^2` is linear in `g`, the whole floor is low by 1.414x in sigma. M4 §8.2 had already measured this from darks (ISO 50 and ISO 100 give **0.9866** and **0.9845** DN, ratio **1.0021**, where the relation demands 0.5) and §8.3 called the implied 8.62 e- read noise "visibly nonsense ... the tell". M25 then measured `g` independently **from signal** by photon transfer: **0.2342** (`119MSDCF`) and **0.2583** (`coffee-bean`) against the relation's 0.11447, with an ISO-160 control recovering 0.3273 vs 0.3663. Dark frames constrain only the product `RN_e*g`, which is exactly why this presented as a read-noise defect. | **Taking the original advice would have shipped a second defect.** Changing `RN_e` fixes the dark case and mis-models the shot term, which dominates on every illuminated frame — a repair fitted on the one channel that cannot see the cause. **FIXED IN SHIPPED CODE** (`2a4f5c5`): `CameraProfile` gains a `base_iso` field and `gain_dn_per_e` clamps to it, so this is data rather than logic per §4.1. Negative control run; 104/104 core tests pass. This also **closes the PTC that §4.1 and open question 5 have owed since M4**. The boundary is NOT measured — the corpus has no ISO 64 or ISO 80 capture — so `max(ISO, 100)` is the simplest rule consistent with the evidence, not a located transition. **Facts 130 and 241 both compute with the old `g` at ISO 50 and are contaminated; M47 is auditing the full blast radius.** | M25 §7 fact 200 (**CORRECTED**, superseding the version first folded here) + M4 §8.2/§8.3 — **MEASURED on two independent channels** |

| 1182 | **THE OPTICAL CUTOFF CANNOT BE MEASURED FROM THE EXISTING CAPTURES, AND THE OBSTACLE IS IDENTIFIABILITY RATHER THAN PRECISION.** M88 built a validated slanted-edge instrument and could not adjudicate 87 against 106-135 cy/mm. Edge rise obeys `rise^2 = d^2 + c^2`: one measurement, two unknowns, and the subject-softness term `c` (~30 um) is **3x larger** than the diffraction term `d` (7-12 um). Every candidate cutoff fits exactly. Even granting a shared `c`, the two hypotheses separate by **1.09 um** against **2.23 um** within-stack scatter. The only assumption-free bound is **`f_c` >= 31.8 cy/mm**, which excludes neither. | **A negative result that names its blocker as the data rather than the method, and proves it.** The instrument was validated **model-free to 114.6 cy/mm from a 48.83 cy/mm sublattice** -- so it can see above the sensor Nyquist of 97.66 cy/mm, which a grid-sampled power spectrum provably cannot; **it simply has nothing sharp enough to point at**. The distinction matters because a precision problem is answered by more frames or better fitting, while an identifiability problem is answered **only** by a different capture, and no amount of analysis will substitute. | MEASURED -- M88, `docs/research/M88-optical-ceiling.md`; nine controls, instrument validated to **+1.19% +/- 1.50%** on planted 60-140 cy/mm |

| 1281 | **THE ANISOTROPY INSTRUMENT PASSES FIVE CONTROLS, AND THREE OF THEM FAILED FIRST AND CHANGED ITS DESIGN.** Final state on `bee-3-cpl-g0`: sensitivity (a planted 10 px radial smear drives A_outer **0.6337 -> 0.0159**), monotone dose order (**0.6337 / 0.4457 / 0.0812 / 0.0159** at 0/1/3/10 px), specificity (a planted isotropic Gaussian of sigma 1.6 moves it only **-0.0113**), a built-in null (**A = 1.0224** at r=0.05 untreated, as the geometry requires), and geometry (at 1 px the outer annuli fall **0.188** against **0.041** at the centre, **4.6x** harder outside). | The specificity arm is the load-bearing one: without it the metric would have been a softness detector wearing an orientation costume. Forming the ratio inside a magnitude ring and averaging afterwards makes the cancellation exact. Two further controls failed and were also design faults rather than results: see disciplines 629 and 630. | ORCH (MEASURED, 5 controls on real captures); `experiments/ORCH-drift-check/anisotropy.py` |

| 1282 | **THE 0.9315 COVERAGE CROP IS NOT IMPOSING A HARD BAND LIMIT ON THE RENDER.** `merge_cmd.rs:1245` reports that the field of view is scaled to 0.9315 so every frame covers every pixel, "then upsampled to keep the output dimensions", which predicts a spectral cliff at **0.4657 cyc/px**. | 1400 | **EVERY ALIGNED RENDER IS UPSAMPLED, AND ON `bee-3-cpl` THE FACTOR IS 1.0735x.** The tool prints `coverage : field of view scaled to 0.9315 so that EVERY frame covers every pixel (6.9% of width dropped, then upsampled to keep the output dimensions)`, and `--help` states `the field of view shrinks ~7-10%`. `align_cmd.rs:1339` documents the mechanism in its own words: *"the field of view shrinks by `k`, and because the output keeps its pixel dimensions the result is upsampled by `1/k`. That couples this directly to facts 1373-1374, where the kernel was measured at **-0.2360 dex** of high-band loss and confirmed by eye. **The upsample is part of what makes the kernel choice bite.** The owner pixel-peeps at 100%, and at 100% they are looking at a 107% view of the real data. | `crates/strehl-cli/src/align_cmd.rs:1339` (source); `merge_cmd.rs:1261`; tool output on bee-3-cpl (MEASURED) |

| 1412 | **THE CORPUS'S STRUCTURAL GATE COULD NOT PRINT THE VIOLATIONS IT FOUND, AND FAILED IN A WAY THAT READ AS A BROKEN TOOL.** `corpus_lint.py` renders each violation with the offending corpus line attached. Python selects the ANSI codepage (`cp1252` here) for **redirected or piped** stdout, and cp1252 cannot encode `\u0394`, `\u2212`, `\u2264` or `\u2192` -- all of which are ubiquitous in this corpus. `print(v.render())` therefore raised `UnicodeEncodeError` **mid-loop**. Measured A/B against HEAD with `PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252` and stdout captured: pre-fix **rc=1, violations printed = 0, no `FAIL` summary, 656 B of traceback**; post-fix **rc=1, violations printed = 7, 0 B of stderr**. Both arms agree there are 7 violations; only one arm can say so. | **The defect was invisible in the only mode a human uses and active in the only mode an agent uses.** Run interactively on a UTF-8 console it printed all seven; run with output captured -- every agent invocation, and any CI log -- it printed **none of them** and exited 1. | 1438 | **AN ARTEFACT AUDIT WITHOUT AN UNSTACKED CONTROL IS MOSTLY MEASURING THE SCENE: A CONTROL KILLED 3 OF 5 "DEFECTS" I FOUND.** An 8-check battery with thresholds registered before the run was put over the two HEAD renders (`lavendar-cpl`, `dry-erase-marker-head-cpl`, 7040x4688) and reported five FIRED. | 1467 | **THE RESAMPLER IS UPSTREAM OF THE ELECTION, SO A KERNEL A/B IS NOT COMPARING THE SAME PHOTOGRAPH: 8.084 % OF QUADS ELECT A DIFFERENT FRAME.** `merge_cmd.rs::field_for` warps **before** it reads a pixel, so the kernel feeds the focus field, the gate and the election. The binary's own printed statistics move (mean `n_eff` 55.321 -> 53.674; winner response median 4.1675 -> 4.2580), and `--index-map` shows **5.643 % of quads shifting by more than one frame, mean \|delta index\| 55.24, max 298**, plus a flat-field level shift of **+8.83 and +8.78 DN** in two independent ROIs. Stratifying by election agreement: **+0.0968 dex where agreement >= 0.99, +0.0604 where < 0.95**, with `corr(agreement, gain)` **+0.30** at 128 px and **+0.41** at 256 px. | **The direction is favourable and that is what makes this a constraint rather than a refutation: the gain is *larger* where the election held still, so the kernel earns it and the re-election dilutes it.** Had the correlation pointed the other way, the entire measured gain would have been attributable to a reshuffled election rather than to interpolation. **Any future end-to-end kernel comparison must report this split** -- and fact 1374's `nearest` comparison needs it most, since `nearest` will perturb the election harder than lanczos3 does. It also means the flat-field level shift is unmodelled: the stack fits no per-frame gain term, which is the photometric-normalisation gap the external review named and M97 has now wired behind `--photometric`. | M113-kernel-verify section 6; `--index-map`, `k3_diagnose.json` |

| 1468 | **"4 OF 4 CONTROLS PASSING" WAS 1 OF 4: TWO CANNOT FAIL AND THE DISCRIMINATING ONE REWARDS RINGING.** Every published reading reproduces exactly -- the arithmetic is honest, the **power** is not. C1 (interpolating) is sound and Mitchell really does fail it. **C2 (partition of unity) has zero power: the weights are divided by their sum three lines above the assertion.** Measured un-normalised the defect it exists to detect is **5.701e-3**; measured through the normaliser it is 2.384e-7 against a 1e-6 bar -- **the normaliser removes it by 23914x**, and what passes is f32 rounding of a six-term sum clearing float epsilon by 4.2x (rule 20). **C3 (support) has zero power: `if x.abs() >= 3.0 { return 0.0 }` sits six lines above it.** **C4, the only discriminating one, is an unbounded ordering on passband gain and ranks a 137 %-overshoot kernel first** -- it prefers every *more* ringing kernel. Separately, fact 1420's claim that a verified patch was "carried verbatim" is false: `align.rs` carries different source. | **A control that asserts a property the code guarantees a few lines earlier is not a weak control, it is a decoration**, and counting it in a score inflates confidence precisely where confidence is least earned. The test is mechanical and should be routine: **for each control, name the concrete change that would make it fail; if you cannot, it has no power.** C4 is the more instructive failure -- it is not powerless but *anti-correlated*, an ordering statistic pointed at a quantity that increases with the artefact being guarded against. **A discriminating control that ranks the worst candidate first would have licensed exactly the wrong kernel had the ladder contained one.** This is the same family as fact 1457's two-bin Spearman and fact 1463's impossible radius: three instruments in one night that returned a confident number while measuring nothing, or the wrong thing. | M113-kernel-verify section 7; `k4_controls.json` |

| 1470 | **THE WAXY-BLOB ARTEFACT IS THE GATE'S ADMISSION TOLERANCE BEING ABSOLUTE WHILE THE FOCUS RESPONSE IS CONTRAST-SCALED.** The tolerance is a fixed **0.086063** in focus-response units (`4.0*sqrt(2)*FOCUS_NOISE_SD`), but the response it is compared against spans **0.43 to 84** with contrast. | 1471 | **BOTH HYPOTHESES I HANDED M111 WERE REFUTED, AND THE REAL SMOOTHER IS A DIFFERENT CONSTANT IN A DIFFERENT FILE.** H1 blamed the spatial regulariser: at `REGULARISER_RADIUS = 0` the plateaus **survive at 54.0 px** against 60.3 px shipped, with amplitude flat across a **32x** range of radius (1.213 / 1.239 / 1.203). Its premise was separately false -- **0.00 %** of either ROI lies below the noise ceiling (medians 4.31 and 2.96 against 0.478). The actual smoothing scale is `focus.rs WINDOW_RADIUS = 13`, a **27x27** window. H2 was refuted as a diagnosis too, and backwards: the gate fires **hardest** where H2 predicted it would not (median `n_eff` **285** in the weakest band, **151** across flat regions). **Fact 84 is not implicated in this artefact.** | **I named two mechanisms and both were wrong, which is the outcome the brief was designed to make cheap rather than embarrassing.** The refutations cost one parameter sweep and one median each, because the brief demanded a falsifiable premise per hypothesis rather than a hunt for supporting evidence. Worth recording specifically: **H1's premise was checkable before H1 was tested**, and checking it first would have killed the hypothesis for free -- 0.00 % of the ROI below the noise ceiling means the regulariser has nothing to act on there. **Test the premise before the mechanism; premises are usually one query and mechanisms are usually a sweep.** The deeper lesson is that I reached for the most recently interesting constant (fact 84's regulariser, priced at -35 %) rather than the one with the right spatial scale, and 27x27 was sitting in a file I did not look at. | M111-waxy-blobs section 2; sweep over `REGULARISER_RADIUS`, `focus.rs WINDOW_RADIUS` |

| 1472 | **A CONTROL THAT REMOVED THE MECHANISM ENTIRELY STILL SCORED 1.686 ON THE STATISTIC THAT WAS ABOUT TO BE THE ANSWER.** M111's first diagnosis rested on blob boundaries coinciding with election boundaries. At `--gate 1e5` the election **cannot** affect the output at all -- yet boundary-coincidence still read **1.686**. The statistic was measuring the fact that both maps have boundaries in the same textured places, not that one causes the other. **Coincidence is not attribution**, and this also **qualifies fact 1445's immunity claim**, which rested on the same kind of reasoning. | **This is the strongest single control result of the night, because it killed a conclusion its own author had already reached.** The design principle it demonstrates is the one that separates a control from a sanity check: **the control must disable the proposed mechanism while leaving everything else in place, and the statistic must then go to null.** A statistic that survives the removal of its own cause is measuring a confounder -- here, that texture drives boundaries in both maps independently. Note the family resemblance to facts 1457, 1463 and 1468: **four instruments in one night returned confident numbers while measuring the wrong thing**, and in every case the catch came from a control rather than from inspecting the number. The replacement evidence (`D = luma(gate 4) - luma(gate 1e5)`, fact 1470) is causal by construction because it differences two renders that differ *only* in whether selection happened. | M111-waxy-blobs section 1; the `--gate 1e5` control |

| 1809 | MEASURED | ORCH | **A PER-BAND NOISE FLOOR DECOUPLES COARSE AVERAGING FROM FINE DETAIL, WHICH `--pyramid-gate` CANNOT DO BY CONSTRUCTION, AND IT IS COMMISSIONED WITH A BYTE-EXACT NULL.** `--pyramid-gate` *"takes a single value by construction"* (`main.rs:236`), so fact 1808's conflict has no expressible answer in the shipping flags. Scaling `k` per band and scaling the floor per band are the same operation, so the knob was added at the cheaper seam: `STREHL_GATE_FLOOR_SCALE`, a comma-separated per-band multiplier in `gatefloor.rs`, **touching no file any other lane owns and requiring no change to the merge**. The instrument that can kill it is the rim axis, not the banner. |

| 1817 | DISCIPLINE | ORCH | **EVERY PRINT-GATE AXIS IS STRUCTURAL, AND A SATURATED REGION HAS NO STRUCTURE, SO A MASTER CAN READ CLEAN ON ALL FOUR WHILE BEING A WHITE SHEET.** Rim, sharpness, dust and cert all score relationships between neighbouring pixel values; when 92% of pixels are pinned at the same value those relationships are gone, and their absence scores as their being in order. This is why an 11-of-18 blowout survived a gate that was passing 17 subjects. **THE RULE: any gate built on differences between pixels must carry a companion check on the pixels themselves -- level, clip fraction, black fraction, median -- because a degenerate image is the quietest possible input to a difference operator.** Corollary for attribution, and it cuts against three of this project's own findings: clipping manufactures infinitely sharp edges (candidate cause of "master exceeds its own focus ceiling" on 13/19 subjects), pins pixels at `hi` (which is definitionally what `pinned_to_hull` counts), and places a blown highlight beside a dark edge (which reads as large overshoot, i.e. rim). Those three measurements were taken on the delivered pin masters, which are **not** blown, so they are not withdrawn -- but any future re-measurement at HEAD must state its clip fraction beside its verdict or the verdict is uninterpretable. |

| 1834 | MEASURED | ORCH | **EVERY RENDER IS UPSAMPLED, NO FRAME IS EVER PIXEL-EXACT INCLUDING THE REFERENCE, AND THE PENALTY GROWS WITH STACK DEPTH.** `fit_to_cover` (`crates/strehl-cli/src/align_cmd.rs`, doc L2225-2244, fn L2245) composes a uniform scale `k <= 1` about the plane centre into **every** frame placement so the reference grid maps strictly inside every source frame. Because the output keeps its pixel dimensions, the result is **upsampled by 1/k**. The doc comment states this outright and calls the alternative -- cropping -- follow-up work deferred because it "would break the byte-frozen measurement path". Measured from the `coverage` banner line at `3a312ba6`: `109MSDCF` N=22 -> **k = 0.9870** (1.3% of width dropped then upsampled); `bee-1-cpl` N=299 -> **k = 0.9321** (6.8%). Two consequences neither lane had isolated. (a) k SHRINKS AS N GROWS, because more frames accumulate more drift to cover, so there is an unconditional **N-dependent resampling blur** in every render, worst on the deepest stacks -- which are the showcase images. (b) Since `S_k` is composed into every placement, the reference frame, which would otherwise pass through untouched, is resampled too, so **no output pixel anywhere is uninterpolated**. This is a testing convenience charged to print quality. Candidate root cause for the owner's standing softness complaint; BUILD-CROP is implementing an opt-in unity-scale crop mode and V-REVIEW holds the adjudication. |

| 1843 | MEASURED | V-NEVERWORSE | **THE N-DEPENDENT SOFTENING IS THE SELECTION PREMIUM, NOT DILUTION OF THE WINNER'S SHARE.** ORCH hypothesised that `SoftPower` normalisation dilutes the best frame's weight as near-ties multiply with N, so deep stacks drift toward an average. **Refuted by a control the hypothesis cannot survive:** an argmax arm has winner share exactly 1.000 and `n_eff` exactly 1.000 at every N, verified to 1e-9, so it **has no dilution to have** -- and it still softens **105 percent** (coffee-bubbles) and **98 percent** (112MSDCF) as much as the shipping merge. THE MECHANISM: on a synthetic twin carrying identical scene content, independent noise, and **no focus signal at all**, selecting rather than averaging multiplies manufactured 0.30-0.35 noise power by **2.16x, 6.79x, 24.82x** at N=4/9/19 (coffee-bubbles) and **23.24x, 80.78x, 240.70x** at N=19/39/79 (112MSDCF). Every selecting arm grows noise about **1.6x faster than signal** (shipping, N=4 to 19: signal 1.476x, noise 2.419x). The plain mean is **the only N-invariant arm**, SNR flat at 0.68/0.68/0.69. This is the max-of-N order statistic operating on a noisy focus measure, so ANY reduction in selectivity helps flat regions while the premium keeps growing with N. CAVEAT STATED BY THE LANE: corr(dilution, softening) is −0.929 on coffee-bubbles but only −0.155 on 112MSDCF, so it does not replicate and must not be quoted; the refutation rests on the argmax control alone. Corroboration from the same round, in the opposite direction: BUILD-SOFTGATE had already deleted its scratch before the order arrived, and rather than assert it was fine it grepped **HEAD** (not the working tree) for twelve key values -- four render hashes, the contaminated hash, both freeze hashes, two pixel counts, three depth figures, the inertness denominator and the second-pass timing -- and got True on all twelve. The discipline earned: **a lane may only call an artifact regenerable after naming the specific inputs the regeneration needs and confirming those inputs still exist**, and the safe default for anything whose inputs are outside the lane's own directory is to bank it as text. | 1948 | ORCH | MEASURED | Fourth occurrence of `an instrument's input path is part of its calibration`, and the first where the orchestrator was the one calibrated wrongly. The print gate run over `DELIVER-V6\masters` returned a partition that summed correctly -- 17 PASS, 0 FAIL, 3 ACQUITTED, 6 ACQUITTAL EXPIRED, 0 REVIEW, 7 NOT EXAMINED, 33 total (found 33) -- while reporting `FileNotFoundError` for exactly the 7 subjects added last. The product had been split across two sibling directories: a concurrently running lane moved those 7 masters into `DELIVER-V6\orch-rendered-7` at 03:38, after an earlier orchestrator count of 33 in `masters` at 02:47 had already been used to certify coverage. Both readings were correct when taken; the tree moved between them. Re-running the gate against the second directory scored all 7 as REVIEW, giving a true 33-subject partition of 17 PASS, 0 FAIL, 3 ACQUITTED, 6 ACQUITTAL EXPIRED, 7 REVIEW, 0 NOT EXAMINED. Two lessons. First, the gate's insistence that every input land in a counted outcome is what surfaced this at all -- a gate that silently globbed would have reported 26 clean masters and no gap. Second, in a tree shared with concurrent agents, a directory listing is a measurement with a timestamp, not a standing fact, and coverage certified from an earlier listing must be re-measured rather than carried forward. |

| 1952 | BUILD-PLUGIN | MEASURED | Pluggability against the brief, stated exactly: ONE of the five plugin kinds the owner asked for is a genuine dispatch boundary, and it is refused on the shipping default. Focus measures are a real trait seam -- `FocusMeasure` at `strehl-core/src/focus.rs:619`, `Registry` at `strehl-plugin/src/registry.rs:216`, CLI adapter `focus_plugin.rs:62` -- and it is demonstrated rather than merely compiled: `strehl focus list` host-measures seven operators live over 12 seeds at 512x512, spanning 10.27x in noise sd with `sml-w13` at 6.61x the default, and swapping the operator on identical input moves 24,702,381 of 24,724,512 samples (99.9105%) between two named hashes while the default output stays byte-identical across three runs and both byte-freezes hold. The noise sd is MEASURED by the host, not declared by the operator, because the trait has no method that could declare it. Against that, merge strategies are an enum match in core (`MergeBackend`, `merge_cmd.rs:271`), and alignment models, optical profiles and output stages have no trait at all. The load-bearing caveat: `--focus` is REFUSED on `MergeBackend::Pyramid` (`main.rs:973-976`), which is `DEFAULT_MERGE_BACKEND`, because the pyramid elects per-band coefficients from band energy and computes no focus field for an operator to replace. Refusing is the right failure over silently ignoring, but it means the plugin surface and the shipping path do not currently intersect. The registry is also in-tree, so a third party cannot contribute a focus measure without patching this repository. |

| 1973 | ORCH-drift-check | MEASURED | AN EXTENSION FILTER THAT IS A PROPER PREFIX OF THE REAL EXTENSION RETURNS A SILENT ZERO, and it fired on the final verification of the deliverable itself. The orchestrator's product check used `Get-ChildItem -File -Filter '*.tif'` against the master directory and printed `masters: 0 TIFFs` while 33 masters totalling 6.08 GB were present, because the files are named `.tiff`. Measured directly on the same directory in the same shell: `-Filter '*.tif'` gives 0, `-Filter '*.tiff'` gives 33, `-Filter '*.tif*'` gives 33, `-Include '*.tif'` gives 0, and a Where-Object test on `.Extension -in '.tif','.tiff'` gives 33. PowerShell's `-Filter` is passed to the filesystem wildcard engine and does NOT extend a trailing extension the way an eye does. The product was then re-verified the correct way and is intact: 33 of 33 SHA256 hashes match the banked table, 0 mismatches, 0 not-in-bank. The generalisable rule is the same one the corpus has now hit from four directions: A ZERO IS THE SAME GLYPH WHETHER THE SET IS EMPTY OR THE QUERY NEVER MATCHED, so any probe whose passing state is a count must be shown to produce a non-zero on a case known to exist before its zero is believed. Enumerate by attribute, not by a hand-typed wildcard, whenever the answer is load-bearing. |

| 1974 | V-H2H2 | MEASURED | THE CONFIDENCE EXPONENT IS A NULL: its cost is measured and its benefit is not quotable. On bee-1-cpl at N=299 with the srgb path, over the acuity band 0.17-0.25 cyc/px where this subject qualifies SIGNAL, arm S100 reads flat 0.8015 and acuity 0.9939; arm S1000 reads flat 0.8052 and acuity 0.8854; arm K (gate floor 4x) reads flat 0.0937 and acuity 1.0028. All three nulls land inside the 0.005 tolerance at 1.0016, 1.0040 and 1.0013, so all three comparisons are valid rather than merely reported. 292. **An experiment whose expected answer is "no" needs an estimator that can return zero, and a placebo that proves it does.** Cross-half covariance has exactly this property -- temporal noise contributes zero in expectation and the estimate may go negative -- which is what makes a null from it worth something. M50's placebo sits at **1.2%** of its plant amplitude, and that row is what licenses believing its null. Without it, "there is no row banding" and "this estimator cannot see row banding" are the same output. This extends rule 11's placebo requirement from defects to nulls.

589. **DISTINGUISH AN IDENTIFIABILITY FAILURE FROM A PRECISION FAILURE BEFORE SPENDING ANYTHING ON PRECISION.** M88 could not separate 87 from 106-135 cy/mm not because its instrument was imprecise -- it was validated to **+1.19% +/- 1.50%** and reaches **114.6 cy/mm** from a 48.83 cy/mm lattice -- but because `rise^2 = d^2 + c^2` has two unknowns and one measurement, with the nuisance term 3x the signal. **More frames, better fitting and longer runs cannot repair an under-determined system; only a different capture can.** The diagnostic is cheap and should precede any measurement campaign: **write down the model, count the unknowns against the independent measurements, and check that the quantity of interest is separable from its nuisance terms at the available scatter.** (SYNTHESIS facts 1182, 1183.)

590. **PREFER AN INSTRUMENT WHOSE NULL IS A THEOREM TO ONE WHOSE NULL IS A CALIBRATION.** M89's fourth-difference kernel annihilates any cubic exactly, so `E[z^2] = 1` follows from the algebra and the measured null landed at **0.9897 with nothing tuned**. 591. **WHEN A DELIVERABLE FAILS ITS BARS, ASK WHICH *STAGE* THE DEFECT LIVES IN BEFORE RE-SPECIFYING THE DELIVERABLE.** M89 was asked for a Wronski-shaped robustness weight on the merge average. 595. **A POWER CONTROL IS MANDATORY FOR ANY INSTRUMENT WHOSE HEADLINE IS AN ABSENCE.** M91 retired *two* of its own instruments this way: handed a disturbance that was uniform by construction, they failed to detect it on 6 of 6 stacks. 598. **A CONTROL THAT READS EXACTLY ZERO IS THE MOST DANGEROUS RESULT IN AN INSTRUMENT, NOT THE MOST REASSURING.** M88b reports that **three of the five defects it found in its own design were controls reading exactly `0.000` that looked like passes.** Exact zero is what a correct null looks like *and* what a disconnected probe, an unreached branch and a self-cancelling comparison look like. **Pair every zero-reading null with a positive control on the same wiring**: M88b cut its treatment set from 5 ROIs to 3 after finding **two that passed the null and were blind to a planted effect**. 600. **A BYTE-IDENTICAL RESTORE IS NOT A RESTORED CONTROL, BECAUSE THE BUILD SYSTEM NEVER SAW IT CHANGE.** M90 planted a defect, restored the source with `shutil.copy2`, confirmed the file was **byte-identical to HEAD** -- and its bars stayed red. `copy2` preserves mtime **by design**, so `cargo` concluded nothing had changed, skipped the rebuild, and **left the planted binary live underneath clean source**. Every source-level check passed while the artefact under test was still the mutated one. It was caught only by re-running the control externally. This is discipline 592 in a new costume -- the verification inheriting the blind spot of the thing it verifies -- and it generalises past `cargo` to every cached build system. **Restore must invalidate the cache, not merely restore the bytes** (touch the file, or force the rebuild), **and the restoration must be proven by re-running the control, never by comparing source.** (SYNTHESIS fact 1210; M90 round 2 N4.)

601. **MEASURE THE STATISTIC THE CONSUMER ACTUALLY SEES, NOT THE ONE THAT IS EASY TO AVERAGE.** `rho_warp` averaged over all frame pairs is **3.4x** too optimistic, because `Estimator::fold` admits an **interval around the winner** and therefore only ever sees the near-pair end of `rho(d)`, where correlation is at its highest. The all-pairs mean is not a conservative simplification of that -- it is a different population, and it is biased in the direction that matters. Before averaging over a population, **state which members the consumer is exposed to and average over those.** (SYNTHESIS fact 1211.)

605. ~~**A GLOBAL SHARPNESS METRIC CAN BE ANTI-CORRELATED WITH IMAGE QUALITY, BECAUSE MISREGISTRATION MANUFACTURES GRADIENT ENERGY.**~~ **RETRACTED, fact 1250.** The premise was the orchestrator's visual claim that the registered render is sharper; that claim was a 1.25% magnification artefact and has been withdrawn. With it withdrawn the metric and the eye agree, and there is no measured instance of anti-correlation. The *mechanism* remains plausible -- a doubled edge does carry two gradients -- but it is now ARGUED with no supporting observation, and no milestone may build on it. (facts 1235, 1237, 1250)

606. **BEFORE COMPARING TWO RENDERS BY EYE, CHECK THAT THEY HAVE THE SAME FIELD OF VIEW, BECAUSE MAGNIFICATION READS AS SHARPNESS.** The orchestrator judged `bee-3`'s aligned render 'dramatically better' than the unaligned one at thumbnail scale and was wrong to: `fit_to_cover` gives the aligned render a ~7% smaller field of view, so at matched output size it renders larger, which reads as sharper for reasons unrelated to registration. The correct comparison is against a field-of-view- and resampler-matched null with only the effect under test removed. This is the visual form of the ordinary confound, and it fooled the person who wrote the rule about it.

610. **A CAVEAT DOES NOT STOP A WRONG NUMBER FROM BEING USED, SO PREFER NOT TO SHIP IT.** The orchestrator folded `leg-spines 1.1288` explicitly flagged unverified and handed it to M97 with the caveat attached; it was the headline evidence that the sharpness metric reverses by region, and it was an artefact of a 1.25% magnification difference. An unverified number that supports the author's thesis will be read as support and the flag will be read as modesty. Either verify it before folding or state the mechanism that would make it wrong, so the reader can check it instead of discounting it. (facts 1237, 1250)

613. **AFTER BUILDING A MASK, ASSERT THAT IT CONTAINS THE THING YOU ARE LOOKING FOR, BEFORE COMPUTING ANYTHING THROUGH IT.** Three masks in one session excluded the artifact they were built to find, and each would have returned a confident wrong answer. Selection criteria correlate with the target more often than is comfortable -- a smoothness criterion excludes steps, a darkness criterion excludes bright defects, a background criterion excludes anything on the subject. Pick a probe region you already believe contains the target, assert coverage, and let it abort. Three lines. (fact 1256)

615. **A PLANT MUST NOT PERTURB THE MECHANISM IT IS MEASURING THROUGH.** A 40% brightness ramp planted to amplify a brightness artifact instead captured the election -- the brightest frames won everywhere, the elected field went constant, and the artifact vanished. The plant was applied upstream of a decision, so it changed the decision rather than the decision's consequence. Before planting, ask what the estimator does *differently* in the presence of the plant; if the answer is 'it chooses differently', freeze the choice first and plant downstream of it. (fact 1260)

624. **PowerShell's `[int]` rounds half to even, so `[int](3/2)` is `2`.** `$v[[int]($v.Count/2)]` on a sorted 3-element array returns the **max** and calls it the median; M97's timing harness reported **29.51 s** for a set whose median is **21.67 s**. 632. **Two independent routes to the same mechanism is worth more than either measurement's error bar, and it is what licenses acting instead of measuring again.** The coverage rescale was found twice in one night by authors who had not seen each other's work: M98 optically, recovering k = 0.9315 from a photograph of a ruler at 0.68σ, and the orchestrator spectrally, pricing that same operation at 64.2% of a deficit measured against an independently decoded RAW. Neither alone would have justified changing the output path -- the orchestrator had already been wrong twice the same night, on the half-drift (fact 1280) and on binning (fact 1284), each time with a plausible single line of evidence. 738. **A control that cannot go red is worse than no control, and controls can poison themselves.** M109's cache-visibility control forced a solve in one arm — **and that arm wrote its warpmap into the redirect directory**, so on re-run the supposedly cache-blind arm read back its own output, both arms took the sidecar path, and `A == B` became **vacuous while still printing green**. It was caught only because the harness carried an explicit **inertness guard** that printed `CONTROL INERT` and hard-failed. The general shape: **any control with a side effect on the state it controls for will converge to passing**, and passing is indistinguishable from working. Every control needs (a) a state reset per arm and (b) an assertion that the perturbation actually perturbed — M109 evidenced its perturbation from `strehl`'s own stderr, `align=solved` **111 s** against `align=sidecar` **63 s**. Compare disciplines 730 and 731: the same failure mode, reached by a different route, for the third time tonight.

739. **When your test set cannot falsify the more aggressive option, ship the conservative one and register the capture that would decide it.** M109's stricter trigger cleared far more magenta (**0.0944 % to 0.0260 %**) but touched **6.56 %** of the frame; it changed **0** strongly-coloured pixels on `marker` and **zero** pixels on `lavendar-cpl`, because *the corpus contains almost no saturated clipped colour*. **A test set that cannot express a risk will always report that risk as absent**, and the better-looking number is exactly when that bias is most tempting. The correct move is neither to ship on unfalsifiable evidence nor to abandon the variant, but to **name the missing capture and defer the decision to it** — recorded in `docs/captures-needed.md`. **Distinguish 'measured safe' from 'unmeasurable here' in the report itself**, or a later reader will read the absence of counter-evidence as evidence.

747. **Assert physical bounds on a derived quantity; do not rely on the verdict computed from it.** A normalised field height above 1.0 passed under `SUPPORT ADEQUATE` (fact 1463), because a verdict is a function of its input and cannot detect that the input is impossible. **Every derived quantity with a known range -- a normalised radius in [0, 1], a correlation in [−1, 1], a fraction in [0, 1], an MTF in [0, 1] -- should be asserted against that range at the point of computation**, which costs one line and catches unit errors, resolution mismatches and axis confusions that no threshold can. Corollary, and it is the more valuable half: **when an unrelated control fails, re-read the output you already accepted.** That is the only routine event that makes an author revisit a result they have stopped questioning, and in this project it has now paid out repeatedly.

767. **When a correction is radial and its fit has empty outer annuli, stratify every headline statistic at the support boundary before believing it.** A whole-frame aggregate silently mixes the fitted zone with the extrapolated one, and for a defect that grows monotonically with radius the **top decile is dominated by precisely the extrapolated pixels** -- so the most impressive number in the report is the one least supported by data. M107's -54.08 % top-decile improvement on `bee-3-cpl` is a materially weaker claim if produced mostly past r = 0.788 than the same number produced inside the fit, and the two cases are indistinguishable in the aggregate. Cost of the split: one mask (facts 1499, 1501).

786. **Weight binned statistics by their support before reading anything off the extremes, because the extreme bins are usually the least-supported ones.** In the CA gain table the highest (1.505) and lowest (1.381) rings carried 52 and 33 windows against up to 240 elsewhere -- **7.4 % of the data defining 100 % of the range**. 788. **Read a fitted artifact's provenance BEFORE interpreting any discrepancy against it.** ORCH measured a 44 % over-correction and concluded 'the coefficient is wrong' without checking which captures the coefficient was fitted from or under what conditions. The profile records both fields, and one of them is explicitly `None` **as information** (fact 1530). **The fitting conditions decide whether a discrepancy means a wrong number or a correctly-fitted number applied out of range** -- and those two diagnoses call for opposite code changes, one of which is a regression.

794. **A mutation that stays inside the defect's own convention cannot reveal the defect.** The independent verifier's mutation testing changed `1/(1+eps)` to `1-eps` -- **both are the same wrong direction**, so the mutant died against tests that were themselves wrong, and the matrix reported health. Mutation testing measures whether tests detect *perturbations of the written code*; it says nothing about a convention error shared by the code and its tests. **Mutation coverage is not a substitute for one measurement in the output domain.**

795. **Verify a correction where its pixels land, not only where its coefficients are fitted.** M107b's sign inversion was caught in a **render-domain preview** after the unit suite was 9/9 green (fact 1536); ORCH's 1.444 scale discrepancy is visible only in the render domain and invisible to a fit reporting `r_squared = 0.9969` (fact 1535). **The same correction has now produced two distinct application-path defects that fit-domain evidence could not see.** Any geometric correction needs at least one end-to-end measurement of the quantity it claims to remove, taken on output pixels.

797. **A detector needs a TRAP it must not fire on, not only a plant it must fire on.** M97r's decisive arm is `defocus` -- the same scene at a different focus -- which a focus-stack robustness mask **must** ignore because that disagreement is the signal. The naive port passed every plant and fired on 100 % of the trap (fact 1541); the obvious fix made the trap ten times worse (fact 1542). **Neither failure is visible without an arm designed to stay silent.** A placebo shows the instrument is quiet on nothing; a trap shows it is quiet on something that looks exactly like the target and is not.

849. **THE ORCHESTRATOR'S FOLD IS AN UNAUDITED TRANSFORMATION, AND ON THE NIGHT IT WAS FIRST AUDITED, EVERY ERROR IN IT RAN THE SAME WAY.** The corpus verifies milestones. It has never verified **the step that turns a milestone's report into a fact**, and that step is performed by the one participant nobody checks. Audited on 2026-08-24/25, six ORCH errors surfaced in a single night: a **synthetic plant's** number folded as *the real occluding scene* (fact 1598); two experiments **spliced**, M86's worst-case half-pixel shift borrowed into M87's warp (fact 1595); a mechanism its own author **explicitly labelled ARGUED** folded as MEASURED (fact 1599); a **700 x 1100 ROI window** folded as *the shipped frame* (fact 1601); **the largest of five numbers** for one effect quoted without the qualifier that gives it meaning (fact 1662); and a default-on recommendation that, on a scan of every document in the corpus, **had no author at all** and had accreted purely in ORCH's summarising (fact 1663). **Not one of the six ran toward weakening a claim. All six ran toward strengthening it.** That is a bias, not a scatter, and its mechanism is plain: summarising drops qualifiers, and a qualifier is almost always what makes a finding smaller. **Consequences.** Fold from the milestone's own primary artefacts rather than from its prose wherever a number is load-bearing; carry the author's own epistemic label (MEASURED / ARGUED) across unchanged, because downgrading it is a finding and upgrading it is a fabrication; name the scene, the space and the window in the same sentence as the number; and **treat the fold as a workstream that requires an independent verifier exactly like any other**, because the rule that an author must not verify their own work has no exemption for the person writing it down.

Compute the ratio *your smallest integration window's spread : the quantisation step*. Below about 10 the statistic is measuring the truncation.

896. **WHEN YOU BROADCAST A HAZARD, STATE ITS DIRECTION AS A HYPOTHESIS AND ASK TO BE CORRECTED -- BECAUSE THE DIRECTION IS THE PART YOU ARE MOST LIKELY TO GET WRONG.** Fact 1746: ORCH broadcast the PIL hazard fleet-wide as a false-null risk, and the first agent to *measure* it found the opposite sign on band-pass statistics. The existence of the hazard was right; the sign was wrong; and a fleet acting on the sign would have dismissed inflated alarms as safe. **A hazard notice carries two claims -- that the mechanism exists, and what it does to your number -- and only the first is usually established when the notice goes out. Label the second ARGUED and invite the measurement.**

900. **A TRAP BEATS A NULL, BECAUSE A NULL CAN ONLY FAIL TO FIND AN EFFECT WHILE A TRAP CAN CONVICT.** Fact 1752: M97e's gate was *null-proven* and still wrong. A null asks `does it do nothing where nothing should happen?`; a **trap** asks `does it do something where doing anything is definitionally an error?` -- and only the second can distinguish a statistic aimed at the right quantity from one aimed at a correlated wrong quantity. Here the trap is a **stationary** stack in which a frame legitimately disagrees because it is the only frame resolving that pixel, so any firing is a false positive by construction. **Register the trap before you build, name what firing on it would prove, and accept that a gate can pass every null you own and still be aimed at the wrong thing.**

903. **BEFORE TRUSTING A CLEARANCE, ASK WHAT THE CHECK WOULD HAVE READ HAD THE DEFECT BEEN PRESENT.** Fact 1754: a census that reads a header field can only ever clear an axis the header records. M117's sidecar header had no smoothing field, so its smoothing clearance was structurally incapable of failing -- and this happened *inside* the audit commissioned to find exactly that class of blindness. **The test is not `did it pass` but `could it have failed`**, and the repair is to re-clear against an artefact that carries the perturbed quantity by construction: whole-file identity over coefficients, not agreement over summaries. This is the same medicine as commissioning a checker with planted defects, applied to a check that was never commissioned at all.
